note: These are proposed criterion designs, not evaluations. Resolve subject-owned thresholds and qualify referenced procedures before activation.

criteria.outcome: A declared consumer obtains the documented core outcome from the distributed artifact in a clean supported environment.
criteria.applicability: APPLICABLE when the selected slice promises distribution to such a consumer; otherwise explicit scope review
procedure: Create an authorized isolated clean environment
Assert the specified externally observable outcome
criteria.thresholds: Read outcome and time/resource budgets from accepted subject profile; no universal numeric threshold is invented.
negative_controls: replace the main command with successful no-op

criteria.outcome: Restoring an accepted backup reproduces the user-data integrity predicates promised for the recovery scenario.
criteria.applicability: APPLICABLE only where accepted or implied data-durability and recovery obligations require restoration; assess scope rather than blanket library/CLI exclusion
procedure: Establish fixture state and integrity baseline
Simulate the authorized failure in isolation
Restore using the real supported path
Evaluate integrity predicates against the restored state
criteria.thresholds: All selected mandatory integrity predicates must hold; recovery time and recovery point are separate scoped criteria.
negative_controls: mock a successful restore without restoring state

criteria.outcome: The product's leading value claim has a concrete beneficiary, observable outcome, credible alternatives and a discriminating experiment.
criteria.applicability: APPLICABLE to active product work seeking further resource allocation; adapt for maintenance-only or archival scopes
review_questions: What observable outcome supports the claim?
What could solve the same problem without this feature or product?
Which smallest authorized experiment would distinguish the alternatives?

anchors.UNASSESSABLE: Required intent or source evidence is unavailable or contradictory without resolution.
anchors.UNSUPPORTED: A benefit is asserted without a testable beneficiary/outcome relationship.
anchors.TESTABLE: Beneficiary, outcome, credible alternatives and a discriminating experiment are specified coherently.
anchors.EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED: A relevant executed experiment supports the claim within explicit limits; does not imply market-wide validation.

negative_controls: generic benefit statement with no observable outcome
experiment whose outcome cannot contradict the claim
